To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rII B starter is activated by termination and requires a (+)-shift on its right to be functional, and that restarting of translation is independent of the distance between the starter and the terminator.
the reinitiation of the polypeptide chains is a phenomenon that is dependent on a mutation in the RII B cistrons.
a mutant which reinitiated the polypeptide synthesis is isolated and the mechanism of its action is investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the genetic code.
a mutant which restarts the polypeptide synthesis of a chain terminator mutant.
the mechanism of chain termination and reinitiation of protein synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mutant x, in the B cistron, permits reinitiation after termination.
a mutant which reinitiated the polypeptide after chain termination is a mutant in which a termination codon has been replaced with a codon which codes for an amino acid.
the starter is a mutant which permits the synthesis of two polypeptide molecules, the second of which is initiated after chain termination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the (+) phase-shift mutation is a conditional amber mutation and that the starter is an amber mutation which is reactivated by a (+) phase.
the reinitiation of a mutant polypeptide chain in the (+) frame is possible only if a (+) phase mutation occurs in the (−)-frame region between the terminator and the reinitiating codon.
reinitiation is a property of the polypeptide chains synthesized by the rII B mutants, not a property of the mutants themselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reinitiation mechanism is a general phenomenon and not a special case of the rII system.
there is a mechanism that can restart the synthesis of a polypeptide after it has terminated.

the restart is independent of the distance between the terminator and the starter, and that the starter can be used to initiate translation in either the (+) or (−) frame, provided the phase of termination is adjusted to match the phase of the starter.
